newsitem.title: INDIA: BT India venture to encourage investors.
newsitem.headline: BT India venture to encourage investors.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT)'s investment in India's Bharti Cellular Ltd (BCL) is likely to encourage foreign investments in the country's telecom sector, officials said on Friday.

"This announcement will be a catalyst to clearing doubts about the speed of reforms in India's telecom sector," Sunil Bharti Mittal, chairman and managing director of the Bharti group, told a news conference.
Earlier on Friday, BT announced it had applied to the Indian government to take over GMC, a subsidiary of France's CGE group with a 22.5 percent stake in Bharti Cellular.
"Delhi is looking a good place to be," BT chairman Iain Vallance told reporters.
"We have been circling around the Indian market for some time and now we have made our first major investment in this sector," Vallance said.
British officials travelling with visiting Prime Minister John Major said the stake would cost British Telecom about 60 million sterling.
A BT executive in New Delhi later confirmed the figure.
Bharti's Mittal said AirTel -- the firm's cellular services brand -- would increase its subscriber base to 350,000 by 2000 from the current 65,000 subscribers.
He said the firm signed on 8,000 users last month and expected to add an additional 8,000-10,000 subscribers this month.
